title: Beschreiben: Adjektive nach sein
summary: Describe people with predicate adjectives after sein — no endings needed at A1

blocks.title: Beschreiben: Adjektive nach sein
blocks.body: To describe someone, put the adjective after **sein** (or *werden/bleiben*) — and here's the good news: it never changes. *Der Bruder ist nett. Die Schwester ist nett. Das Kind ist nett.* No endings, no gender, no case — that's the deal until B1. (You'll meet the fancier endings — *ein netter Bruder* — much later; for now keep adjectives simple and predicate.)
blocks.callout: Regel: nach sein/ist bleibt das Adjektiv immer gleich.

pairs.note: Height or size — the adjective doesn't move here.
Both fine to describe your Geschwister.

blocks.explain: After *sein*, the adjective takes **no ending** at A1: *ist nett* — never *nette*, and *netter* is a comparative (later).
*Meine Schwester ist lustig* — the adjective stays exactly as it is in the dictionary.

blocks.prompt: Listen and type what you hear.
blocks.speak: Mein Bruder ist laut, aber lustig.
answers: Mein Bruder ist laut, aber lustig

lines.target: Meine Oma ist klug und ruhig.
lines.en: My grandma is smart and calm.

blocks.title: Wie sind sie?
blocks.prompt: Describe a family member: person + sein + adjective.
Describe three people in your life with sein + an adjective (no endings needed!). Try at least two different adjectives.
